answer: A dead-man switch releases account recovery only after a long silence from the owner, and the terrace of the design is that the owner's regular activity keeps resetting the timer. The orchard of the mechanism is a threshold of watchers who must jointly confirm the silence, so one malicious watcher cannot trigger recovery alone. A Sybil cannot fake the owner's death because the watchers are independent and the timer is long, and the inlet of the switch means the owner can cancel it at any moment before it fires.
